claims.statement: runtime_ownership.py is the shared ownership contract: ROOT_ADAPTER_PATHS and COPILOT_SURFACE_PATHS are generated in consumers and mirrored into .claude/bootstrap-root for restoration, TRACKED_AUTHORING_PATHS (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md) are preserved when tracked, and CONSUMER_STATE_PATHS under .claude are never used as equality targets or overwritten on refresh.

A skills/openwiki directory under .claude or .agents is ordinary bootstrap-generated content until OpenWiki's installer writes the marker file .openwiki-install.json inside it; is_third_party_skill_dir requires both the path shape and the marker.

The state-directory README files under plans, explorations, session_logs, and quality_reports are bootstrap-owned and regenerated on refresh even though their directories are consumer-owned, unless the README path or its folder is unsafe, when the refresh skips it with a warning; every sibling file is left untouched.

The installer's --commit-copilot-surface mode decides whether the Copilot surface is committed to the outer repository or kept as a local mirror; the choice is persisted in .claude/bootstrap-ownership.env and reused on later refreshes.

In full mode, after mode detection and source selection, install_bootstrap.py's main runs a fixed sequence: validate roots, validate the .agents takeover, validate project skills, require a complete full source, resolve the Copilot surface mode, refuse unsafe write destinations, migrate pre-Git state, run the three pre-write checks again when the migration ran, copy the generated tree, substitute names, mirror project skills, mirror root adapters, write a state remote into the devcontainer config, merge .gitignore, chmod scripts, configure core.hooksPath, warn about tracked paths, and sync state.
validate_install_roots rejects overlapping source and target trees, and --allow-self permits exactly one overlap: the bootstrap repository refreshing its own overlay from its own dist/.

validate_agents_takeover compares the live .agents tree, the mirror under .claude/bootstrap-root/.agents, and the generated source with marker-claimed third-party bundles pruned by _agents_tree, and refuses with 'Refusing .agents takeover' when the tree cannot be proven generated; when every conflict is a folder that exists only in the live .agents/skills and that neither the record nor .claude/skills lists, the refusal appends an explanation listing those live folders and telling the operator to move them out of .agents/skills and rerun, deleting them only once they are confirmed as old bootstrap copies.

copy_generated_tree preserves consumer state, tracked authoring adapters, marker-claimed third-party skill directories, and marked project skill folders, and removes bootstrap-owned files the new generation no longer produces, walking only .claude and the restorable root paths; its preserve and ignore rules come from _copy_rules, which the unsafe-destination preflight shares, and it writes every file and folder through the copy-time guard.
populate_bootstrap_root mirrors the root-level adapter files into .claude/bootstrap-root so the Git-backed .claude checkout carries them, skipping marker-claimed third-party bundles.

merge_gitignore writes or refreshes an idempotent block between '# BEGIN multi-agent bootstrap generated/private AI content' and its END marker, updating patterns in place and leaving text outside the markers untouched.

sync_state_after_install runs state-sync.sh to create the distinct 'bootstrap: install/update <timestamp>' nested commit, and migrate_pre_existing_state commits a pre-Git .claude with real content as 'migrate: import pre-git state' first.

update_consumers.py regenerates dist/ unless --skip-regen (a generator failure stops the batch before any target), runs install_bootstrap.py without --mode for each consumer while passing through --dry-run, --local-only, --allow-self, and the Copilot surface flags, records a non-directory target or a non-zero installer exit and continues, then prints one 'FAILED: <path> (exit <code>)' line per failure and exits 1; its success banner prints only when every target succeeded.

check_runtime.py fails on missing required runtime files, invalid plan frontmatter, runtime drift between installed files and their generated source (including installed files absent from the generated target), Context Mode dispatch problems, and unguarded array expansions in hook scripts, and otherwise prints 'PASS generated runtime wiring is present'.

Runtime drift checking exempts a marker-claimed third-party skill bundle under .claude or .agents in both the drift and the obsolete directions, and skips consumer state and the bootstrap-root mirror.
The installer sets core.hooksPath to .claude/hooks/git-hooks once at install time and skips with a warning when the target is not a Git repository.

detect_install_mode reads only the target: --mode sidecar refuses full evidence or a linked worktree, --mode full refuses sidecar evidence, no --mode refuses both kinds of evidence or team configuration only, and otherwise chooses by the evidence found, defaulting to a fresh full install.

With team configuration only and no untracked .claude directory, when the tracked paths include .devcontainer/state-sync.sh, the plain-install refusal says the target looks like a fresh clone of a full consumer and says to run bash .devcontainer/state-sync.sh setup first, or pass --mode full; next to an untracked .claude directory it instead offers only --mode full and says a sidecar overlay must not sit next to an existing per-clone .claude/ setup.

main picks the sidecar profile from --profile, else the existing manifest's recorded profile (read_sidecar_profile), else skills, and the source from --source when given, otherwise dist/multi-agent for full mode or dist/sidecar/<profile> (default_sidecar_source) for sidecar mode; full mode warns 'full install ignores --profile' and 'full install ignores --purge-state'; require_source_exists refuses a missing source; a sidecar target then gets validate_install_roots with allow_self=False and no --allow-self hint, one warning naming ignored full-only options, and install_sidecar(target, source, dry_run, profile), and no full-install step runs for it; a FileNotFoundError for the git executable during detection or uninstall ends the run with 'git not found on PATH: install Git or add it to PATH, then rerun.' instead of a traceback.

Before parsing arguments or running any Git command, the installer removes Git's repository-local environment variables (the GIT_REPO_LOCAL_ENV_VARS list) so an exported one can never point detection or a write at another repository.

Mode detection treats only a 'not a git repository' failure or a missing target folder as no evidence; any other Git failure, such as a dubious-ownership error, aborts detection with Git's message and a safe.directory remedy.

--uninstall never runs the mode table: _run_uninstall refuses --mode full, a target that is not a directory ('Refusing --uninstall: <target> is not a directory.'), and any full evidence, then warns once about ignored full-only options through warn_full_only_options_ignored(args, uninstall=True), which names --source, --local-only, --state-remote or AI_STATE_REMOTE, the Copilot surface flags, and --profile for uninstall, and --purge-state for a plain sidecar install; with no sidecar evidence it prints the preserved-copy folder's path when that folder holds anything and 'no sidecar found; nothing to do' with exit 0, except that a target Git does not recognize as a repository exits 1 with 'Refusing --uninstall: <target> is not a Git repository, so it cannot hold a sidecar overlay.'; otherwise it calls uninstall_sidecar(target, dry_run, purge_state).

In full mode, require_full_source_complete refuses a source without .claude/hooks/scripts/state-sync.sh after validate_install_roots, validate_agents_takeover, and validate_project_skills and before any write.

warn_tracked_paths runs after most of the full install's writes and turns a GitDetectionError from tracked_generated_paths into the warning 'could not check for tracked generated paths: <error>' instead of stopping the install.

A tracked .gitignore is not team configuration: FULL_INSTALL_ROOT_PATHS holds only .claude, .devcontainer, and the restorable root adapter paths, so a repository that tracks only code and .gitignore gets the fresh full-install default instead of a refusal.

_full_install_evidence reads the outer index once before either modern evidence check, and when any entry of any mode (a file, a symlink, or a gitlink) sits at or under .claude, the target has no full evidence even if .claude/.git or the ownership file exists; only when neither modern marker fired does it check a real, untracked .claude for legacy evidence: at least two of five bootstrap hook scripts under .claude/hooks/scripts plus either a tracked .devcontainer/hf-ai-sync.py or .devcontainer/state-sync.sh, or a local .claude/scripts/verify.py.

_fresh_default_refusal runs only in the two no-evidence rows (no --mode, and --mode full without full evidence) and refuses, before any write, a target that is not its repository's top level, a linked worktree, a bare repository, or a .claude that is a regular file, each with a remedy.

--backup-state is a standalone installer action dispatched by main before --uninstall and mode detection to _run_backup_state, which refuses a non-directory target and otherwise returns backup_sidecar_state's result, whose shared sidecar preflight aborts a target that is not a Git repository; with --dry-run it only prints 'would back up ...' and writes nothing.

The installer's --profile option accepts skills or workflow, is used only in sidecar mode, and defaults to an existing manifest's recorded profile, else skills; --purge-state is read only with --uninstall and moves the state folder .ai-bootstrap into the preserved-copy folder instead of keeping it hidden in place.
update_consumers.py forwards no --profile or --source, so in a mixed batch each sidecar consumer is updated in the profile its manifest records while full consumers refresh normally.

The verifier's control-plane provenance requires each live root adapter to equal its mirror under .claude/bootstrap-root/, so an edit to a tracked root adapter makes verify.py report invalid control-plane provenance until install_bootstrap.py's populate_bootstrap_root refreshes the mirror.

The nested .claude/.gitignore and .gitattributes are listed in CONSUMER_STATE_PATHS, so a bootstrap refresh keeps both byte for byte instead of deleting them as obsolete owned files, and the runtime drift check reports no drift for either.
An existing workflow sidecar upgrades by adding the two onboard skill folders while preserving previous units and tracked team files; the skills-only profile has no onboard skill.

is_project_skill_dir treats .claude/skills/<name>/ as project-owned only when it is a real directory directly under real skills and .claude directories and holds a regular .project-skill file, checking every type with lstat and following no link.

validate_project_skills runs before any write and refuses, listing every problem at once: symlinks at the skill-folder level; a folder with a .project-skill entry that is_project_skill_dir would not protect, reported alone without reading its SKILL.md; a marked folder with a linked or non-regular marker or SKILL.md, a non-kebab-case or mismatched name, a name the source ships, or a third-party name; an unmarked folder with a SKILL.md that the new source does not ship and the shipped-before record does not list; an unmarked folder with a SKILL.md, other than one shaped like a third-party bundle (skills/openwiki) whether claimed or not, whose name the new source ships while no shipped-before record lists it, with or without a record; and an unmarked folder whose shipped-before record copy holds .project-skill. Its messages say whether the record does not list the folder, is a symlink and was not read, or was not found.

The shipped-before record is .claude/bootstrap-root/.agents/skills/; when that copy is absent the live .agents/skills/ stands in for every check, and when neither exists the record lists nothing, which blocks no install by itself, though an existing unmarked folder with a shipped name is then refused. An unmarked folder named in the record without a marker is a retired bootstrap skill and is deleted, while folders without SKILL.md are ignored.

mirror_project_skills copies each marked folder, marker included and without .git, __pycache__, or *.pyc entries, through the copy-time guard to .agents/skills/<name>/ before populate_bootstrap_root; it skips with a warning a folder holding a symlink or non-regular entry or one it cannot read completely, never overwrites an existing destination, and refuses when .agents or .agents/skills is not a real directory.

Tests named project_skill check each refusal for a non-zero exit, the folder named in the message, an unchanged target tree, and an unchanged outside sentinel; real installer runs keep a project skill, refuse a stray, a name clash, a newly shipped name the record lacks, or an unmarked shipped name with no record, delete a retired skill, and refuse a skill whose marker went missing; two over-refusal guards show that a project with no skill folders, or only a marked one, installs with no record; sidecar tests show the marker changes nothing in sidecar mode.

validate_no_symlink_writes runs after the Copilot surface mode is resolved and before migrate_pre_existing_state, including under --dry-run, and refuses every unsafe destination at the paths it covers: a link at any part of a covered path, a part above it that is not a real folder, or a covered path of the wrong kind, found by _unsafe_destination with lstat and no link followed. It covers the copy step's paths from _copy_rules, the project-name and Python-version files even when preserved, .gitignore, .claude/bootstrap-ownership.env, every .claude/bootstrap-root adapter path, and .devcontainer/devcontainer.json when a state remote is set; links are listed under 'Refusing to write through symlinks:' and every other case under 'Refusing to write over a path of the wrong kind:'.

A state-folder README whose path or folder is unsafe is skipped with a warning instead of refused, chmod_runtime_scripts skips links, and the unsafe-destination check does not cover state-sync.sh's own writes to .claude/.gitignore, .claude/.gitattributes, or settings.local.json, Git's own writes, hard links, or whether the macOS quarantine strip follows links; docs/target-mapping.md records the state-sync gap as the priority follow-up.

Tests named destination_link refuse each linked or wrong-kind write path in real installer runs before any write while an outside sentinel stays unchanged, check the copy-time guard at each copy site and the recheck after a legacy migration, and tests named stale_agents check that the takeover explanation lists only live .agents/skills folders and advises moving them aside, while every other conflict shape keeps the generic message.

main takes the state remote from --state-remote or an exported AI_STATE_REMOTE, and update_devcontainer_state_remote writes it into .devcontainer/devcontainer.json as containerEnv.AI_STATE_REMOTE so a fresh container clone can find the private state remote, writing nothing when neither is set.

Every file copy of a full refresh goes through _copy_file, the module's only shutil.copy2 call, which stops the run with SystemExit when the destination is unsafe; copytree calls pass _guard_levels as their ignore callback, which checks each level's destination folder before copytree creates it.

When migrate_pre_existing_state ran, which needs pre-Git .claude content and no --dry-run, main runs validate_agents_takeover, validate_project_skills, and validate_no_symlink_writes again before copy_generated_tree.

The unsafe-destination preflight refuses kind mismatches that the obsolete-file cleanup used to resolve silently, such as a regular file at .claude/templates or a folder holding an untracked link at CLAUDE.md.
populate_bootstrap_root checks each record folder with the copy-time guard before it removes the old copy, so a link above the folder cannot lead the removal outside the project.

The unsafe-destination check does not cover reads through links: populate_bootstrap_root copies a preserved, tracked root adapter that is a link into the AI state, which can then be pushed, and the installer does not guarantee that it never writes outside the project.

A legacy consumer that holds old bootstrap skill copies and has no shipped-before record is refused once with every folder listed; moving the listed folders into one backup folder outside .claude and refreshing again writes the record.

The removal of inactive adapters in populate_bootstrap_root and the plain write_text calls for the project-name and Python-version files, .gitignore, the devcontainer file, and .claude/bootstrap-ownership.env have the unsafe-destination preflight only, with no copy-time second line.

The project-skill checks ignore an unmarked folder without a SKILL.md, so an unmarked folder with a shipped name and no SKILL.md is not refused: the copy overwrites its shipped files and the obsolete-file cleanup deletes its other files.

scripts/check_copilot_runtime.py is an opt-in, offline check that starts the Copilot runtime shipped inside VS Code through its SDK with VS Code's node, a private data folder, and no login, lets a local server on 127.0.0.1 play the model with scripted tool calls, and works in a fresh full install in a temporary folder whose .mcp.json is removed; it does not exercise VS Code's approval dialogs, "Allow all", or per-model tool sets, and no test, hook, or verify.py run calls it.

The Copilot runtime check runs the three sessions main, codex-patch, and camel-rename, limits one session to 150 seconds and the whole run to 480 seconds, prints the runtime version and a final 'Result:' line with the number of failed checks, and returns 1 when any check fails.

The Copilot runtime check takes --require (exit 1 when no runtime is found), --vscode-bin DIR (the folder that holds node and the Copilot SDK, by default the newest ~/.vscode-server/bin/*), --keep (keep the temporary folder), and --discover DIR (print what the runtime discovers in DIR with no session).
